findings.shape: An airy conical selected larch has light-green soft needle clusters on short spurs, single needles on selected longer shoots, pale small twigs, drooping secondary branches and small upright woody seed cones. It is deciduous; a green summer form is displayed.
findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
findings.movement: Same retained woody axes, rachises, leaves and reproductive surfaces during small authored external deflection. Root/support position and scale remain anchored. Timing and angles are qualitative; there is no wind/elasticity solver, physiological simulation or measured biomechanics. Complete germination, organ emergence and seed-to-adult development are unavailable; no resizing of a ready mature plant.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual institutional account through search retrieval: single light-green new-shoot needles versus older spur clusters, straw twigs, erect small cones, straight stem and drooping laterals. corrections: Replaced the repeated generic conifer with irregular primary axes, drooping secondary twigs, short spurs with selected needle tufts and single long-shoot leaf cues.
Changed over-round and separated shelf-like cone scales to a narrower, closed ovoid surface with overlapping rounded laminae.
Added original continuous bark pigmentation and subdued leaf variation; retained every surface during small external branch deflection.
findings.residual: Crown remains too open and regularly branched relative to the retained dense summer photograph. Cone and needle dimensions are selected unmeasured proportions; exact spur counts, scale anatomy, cuticle/stomata and seasonal yellowing/abscission are incomplete. Numerical materials remain visibly stylized.
